URL: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-iran-discuss-phased-deal-reopen-hormuz-end-us-blockade-sources-say-2026-09-24/
Reuters INSIGHT — published 24 Sep 2026 17:18 BST, updated 18:20 BST (by Samia Nakhoul, Parisa Hafezi, John Irish; additional reporting Steve Holland)

HEADLINE: US and Iran discuss phased deal to reopen Hormuz and end US blockade, sources say

US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said.
The strait has become the central bargaining chip in efforts to end the nearly SEVEN-MONTH US-Iran conflict.
Sourcing: two Iranian sources, two regional officials and two Western diplomatic sources.

A senior Iranian official said the most plausible way to end the impasse would be a phased arrangement, with Iran allowing navigation through Hormuz in return for the US lifting its economic blockade and Tehran potentially gaining access to frozen assets.
QUOTE (senior Iranian official, on the sidelines of the UNGA): "One way forward would be to solve the crisis in stages. The first would be to end the blockade and reopen Hormuz."
QUOTE (senior Iranian official): "Our fingers are on the trigger. The Americans know what they need to do but, because of their excessive demands, the chances of diplomacy resolving this are extremely low."

An earlier understanding collapsed in July. Trump has said he thinks the US and Iran could reach a deal after midterm elections to Congress on NOVEMBER 3. A senior European official said the Iranians "have a very long list of demands."

QUOTE (White House official): "Iran is desperate for a deal, President Trump holds all the cards and will make whatever decision is best for the United States." Trump remained "open to talking with Iran under the right circumstances" but had no need to negotiate, and the US was in a "very strong position" with control of the Strait of Hormuz and an Iranian economy that was "collapsing." The official said "crushing sanctions" and "one of the most successful blockades in history" have crippled Iran's economy; Trump was content to let the "inevitable Iranian collapse" play out rather than be "played" by Tehran.

QUOTE (Dennis Ross, former US negotiator): saw only a 30% chance of an agreement being reached before the vote. "The blockade is what's really squeezing the Iranians. It's strangling them."
A deal before the midterms could benefit Trump — reopening Hormuz could ease Gulf tensions, contain oil prices and help bring down politically sensitive US gasoline prices. After the midterms Ross said Trump may face fewer constraints and be more willing to intensify pressure or consider military options.

Regional sources said Tehran was willing to DROP a demand for payment of transit fees to use the Strait of Hormuz from the main agreement and put it in a side attachment instead, as ending the blockade had become the more urgent priority. Gulf states have rejected the transit-fee proposal. Any arrangement would be temporary, not a formal abandonment of Iran's position.

"Iran is not primarily focused on imposing tolls in Hormuz but on preserving its administrative control of the waterway. Iran may be willing to defer the toll issue, but they are not going to give up administrative control of the strait." [NOTE: attribution of this quote is ambiguous in the Reuters text as scraped — DO NOT attribute to a named speaker without re-checking.]

This month the US targeted Iran's remaining commercial airlines and support networks as part of a campaign to sever economic lifelines to the government and the Revolutionary Guards. Trump warned that Iran's economy could "rot" unless it reached a deal.

GULF: During a separate meeting with Trump in New York, Gulf leaders sought clarity on Washington's endgame beyond the midterms, including whether the US would resume military action if Iran refused to return to negotiations. They conveyed their collective rejection of any Iranian control of Hormuz, saying freedom of navigation must be restored and the waterway should not become a tool of coercion against Gulf states.
QUOTE (Ebtessam al-Ketbi, president of the Emirates Policy Center, Abu Dhabi): "It's still not clear what Trump's endgame is, or what the alternative to the pressure campaign would be." And: "The Iranians, by contrast, know what they want. They're reshaping the regional landscape through Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb with a clear objective while Washington has yet to define its roadmap."
Danny Citrinowicz, regional analyst and former Israeli military intelligence officer, said the New York talks had not altered the basic positions of either side and that Iran was unlikely to retreat as long as it believed Trump wanted to avoid a wider escalation before the midterms.
QUOTE (Alan Eyre, former US negotiator on Iran): "The blockade is hurting them, but rather than softening their position, it is likely to drive them to escalate because they believe that if they soften their position, they are dead."
QUOTE (Western official familiar with the talks): "It is all about opening the Strait of Hormuz. We're all under pressure domestically and the Iranians know that."
